title: MCP: Origins and Requests For Startups — Theodora Chu, Model Context Protocol PM, Anthropic
talk_summary: Anthropic's MCP PM recounts MCP's origin and adoption, then lists ecosystem gaps: more high-quality servers, simpler server tooling, and security/observability. The most transferable advice is to design tools around model/user prompts rather than 1:1 API wrappers, add clarification/elicitation, and debug/audit tool servers.

takeaways.technique: Design tools for the model, not as API wrappers
takeaways.what_they_do: They argue MCP servers should be built around end-user prompts and the model's needs, not by exposing every API endpoint one-to-one as a tool.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a lot of people are wrapping their API endpoints one to one and just exposing that as tools. I don't think that's the right way

takeaways.what_they_do: MCP servers can ask end users for clarification when a request is ambiguous, then pass the answer back to the server.
takeaways.evidence_quote: This uh allows servers to ask for more information from end users.

takeaways.what_they_do: They maintain an inspector debugging tool for MCP servers and call it underutilized.
takeaways.evidence_quote: making updates to inspector which if you aren't familiar with is a really good uh debugging tool for for your server.

takeaways.what_they_do: They warn that giving AI applications access to outside systems and real data increases security and privacy implications, making observability/auditing important.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the security and privacy etc implications also go up

takeaways.what_they_do: They optimize MCP for server simplicity and deliberately push complexity into the client when trading off.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we tend to optimize for pushing the complexity down to the client.
